title: Invocation parity auditor for staged traffic (shadow + A/B) with schema diffing
creator: Rina Patel
description: Build an invocation-parity auditing service that runs alongside staged rollouts (shadow and A/B lanes) to detect functional incompatibilities between a candidate model and the active model. The auditor must compare structured outputs and function-invocation signatures at multiple fidelity levels (shape, field-level types, semantic labels) and surface a single diff score used by the rollout controller to mark unhealthy candidates. The goal is to catch regressions in tool-calling and structured output without blocking normal traffic: non-blocking sampling for initial detection and thresholded auto-unwind for severe regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Auditor runs on shadow sink and A/B forks and produces a parity score per request that is stored in telemetry (parity_score: 0..100)

2) Parity scoring evaluates syntactic diffs (field presence/shape) and semantic diffs (enum/value mapping) and exposes component-level breakdowns in telemetry (shape_delta, type_delta, semantic_delta)
3) Rollout controller can consume parity metrics and execute an automatic unwind if sliding-window median parity < 70 for 5-minute windows and error_rate delta > 3x baseline
4) Audit reports include example diffs (golden input, active output, candidate output, diff annotation) and are retained for 30 days in the console under /models/<id>/parity-audit
5) End-to-end latency overhead when auditing in shadow mode remains <2% P95 and does not alter live request SLOs
6) Integration tests that inject synthetic shape/semantic changes fail the candidate automatically in CI and surface the failing diff in the PR summary
progress_updates: 2026-02-22 - Spike: prototyped shape hashing using stable JSON paths and order-independent hashing; found 8% collision risk for large arrays (notes in drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/parity-spike)
2026-02-28 - Design review with PM/DS: agreed to separate syntactic and semantic layers (syntactic quick-check in path-index space; semantic checks use value-normalization + mapping tables)
2026-03-03 - Implemented initial server-side sampler and shadow sink hook; merged shadow sink instrumentation (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12367)
2026-03-08 - Early telemetry dashboard landed in console (internal link: https://console.redwood.ai/models/parity-audit?model=candidate-alpha)
2026-03-11 - QA found a false-positive cluster for minor float rounding differences; added configurable numeric-tolerance bucket and normalization step
risks: Semantic diffing requires curated mapping tables for third-party tool schemas; maintenance burden grows with supported tool surface
High-cardinality outputs (large lists) can inflate diff scores; need sampling and array-collapsing rules
Telemetry volume increase if we persist full diffs for every request; retention cost trade-off vs forensic value
next_steps: Finish semantic normalizer and mapping-table loader (owner: Miguel)
Add CI synthetic tests that mutate function signatures and verify auto-fail behavior (owner: Rina)
Wire parity metrics into rollout controller thresholds and add an opt-in auto-unwind toggle in console (owner: Service Reliability)
Schedule a security review for diff payload retention and PII leakage (owner: Security)
Run a 48-hour shadow sweep on internal models and evaluate false-positive/false-negative tradeoffs
notes: Design decision: favor conservative auto-unwind criteria; we will not auto-block canaries on first detection — action requires sustained low parity + error spike
Related incident: INC-2026-03-02 (candidate release caused tool-call mismatch; parity auditor could have flagged earlier). Postmortem: https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortems/INC-2026-03-02.pdf
Follow-up: explore an opt-in strict-mode for customers that want pre-production blocking audits
